metadata.title: Adaptive laboratory evolution of Escherichia coli W enhances gamma-aminobutyric acid production using glycerol as the carbon source

reference.title: Adaptive laboratory evolution of Escherichia coli W enhances gamma-aminobutyric acid production using glycerol as the carbon source

target.condition: M9 minimal, glycerol sole carbon, 37 C, 200 rpm.

trigger.observation: Glycerol is a non-preferential, low-energy-density carbon source; prior work showed E. coli W among the best GABA producers from glycerol but without optimization (Hou and Kang, 2018).
trigger.reasoning: Adapt E. coli W to glycerol limitation to improve glycerol utilization and growth as a chassis for growth-coupled GABA production.

evidence.description: Doubling time/growth rate trajectory (Fig. 1B/C), specific growth rate, glycerol consumption rate (Fig. 1D).
evidence.source_location: Parental E. coli W grown in parallel assays (growth-rate and glycerol-consumption comparison, incl. M9-glucose reference).

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Outcome measured directly: growth rates, glycerol uptake rates, WGS mutation profiles.
decision_chain.implementation_detail: Serial-batch adaptive laboratory evolution in M9 + 0.2% (v/v) glycerol; 50 mL / 250 mL flask, 37 C, agitation; transfer every 12 h; initial OD600 stepped down 0.0008 -> 0.0004 -> 0.00016; ~1300 generations; single clone CY02 isolated from fittest endpoint lineage on M9-glycerol agar.

result.metric: Doubling time/growth rate trajectory (Fig. 1B/C), specific growth rate, glycerol consumption rate (Fig. 1D).
result.after: Growth rate +~40% (0.67 -> 0.94 /hr); glycerol consumption rate significantly increased; negligible fitness change on glucose (glycerol-specialist adaptation).

decision_chain.rule: When improving an E. coli host for growth-coupled product formation from the low-energy-density feedstock glycerol, apply serial-batch ALE under glycerol limitation (order of 10^3 generations), because selection enriches substrate-uptake/utilization mutations (e.g., glpK, crp) that raise fitness and feedstock conversion, as validated for E. coli W glycerol utilization and GABA production in this study.

trigger.observation: WGS found glpK^m and crp^m shared between endpoint population and CY02 and recurrent across published glycerol/nutrient-limitation ALE experiments; mglC failed validation as hitchhiker.
trigger.reasoning: Test whether glpK^m and crp^m recapitulate fitness benefits in the parental background.

evidence.description: Specific growth rate and specific glycerol uptake rate.

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Fitness and GUR effects measured directly in reconstructed strains; enzyme phenotype confirmed by kinetics (EXP4).

alternatives.approach: ptsP, rsfS and mglC were candidate causal mutations but deprioritized (mglC shown phenotypically neutral; rsfS low recurrence; ptsP role left unresolved)

decision_chain.implementation_detail: Lambda-Red recombineering (Datsenko-Wanner) to construct glpK^m, crp^m singles and glpK^m crp^m double mutant.

result.metric: Specific growth rate and specific glycerol uptake rate.
result.after: glpK^m +1.45-fold growth (p<0.022), +1.78-fold GUR (p=0.02); double +1.56/+1.70; CY02 +1.63/+1.60; crp^m alone not significant; glpK^m accounts for >90% of CY02 fitness increase (Discussion).

target.condition: LB + 2% (v/v) glycerol, 37 C, 200 rpm, 50 mL/250 mL flask.

trigger.observation: Final GABA titers in minimal glycerol medium were negligible and identical between WT and CY02 (0.06 g/L), despite improved glycerol uptake.
trigger.reasoning: Overcome negligible GABA production observed in minimal glycerol medium.
trigger.source_location: WT, glpK^m, crp^m, glpK^m crp^m, CY02 (lacZ:mtGAD)

evidence.description: Final GABA: minimal medium 0.06 vs 0.06 g/L (WT vs CY02, negligible); LB + 2% glycerol: WT 0.05, crp^m 0.06, glpK^m 0.07, glpK^m crp^m 0.07, CY02 0.17 g/L.

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Decisions followed measured titers and measured growth-rate optima (Fig. S7).

alternatives.approach: Continuing in minimal medium with higher glycerol alone (rejected: 0.2% glycerol itself limiting and growth inefficiency persists)

decision_chain.implementation_detail: Switch from M9 + 0.2% glycerol + 50 mg/L yeast extract to amino-acid-rich LB + glycerol; glycerol concentration screen (0-? %; optimum 2% v/v) using growth rate as proxy assuming growth-coupled production; stationary-phase GABA screen of all strains.

result.metric: Final GABA: minimal medium 0.06 vs 0.06 g/L (WT vs CY02, negligible); LB + 2% glycerol: WT 0.05, crp^m 0.06, glpK^m 0.07, glpK^m crp^m 0.07, CY02 0.17 g/L.
result.after: Medium composition identified as integral; CY02 advantage manifests only in rich medium with sufficient carbon.

decision_chain.rule: When growth-coupled production of an amino-acid-derived product (GABA) from glycerol stalls in minimal medium, switch to an amino-acid-rich complex medium and re-optimize feedstock concentration using growth rate as proxy, because biosynthetic precursor (L-glutamate) cost and carbon availability, not uptake capacity, limit product formation - demonstrated for E. coli W GABA production.

target.condition: LB + 2% (v/v) glycerol, 37 C, 200 rpm, 50 mL/250 mL flasks.

trigger.observation: CY02 exhibited pronounced acetate overflow (EXP8) wiring excess substrate influx to acetate; known risk of methylglyoxal accumulation to cytotoxic levels in FBP-insensitive glpK backgrounds; GABA shunt recycles product into TCA.
trigger.reasoning: Redirect acetate-overflow and bypass fluxes toward GABA production.

evidence.description: Growth (lag phase prolonged in ΔackA strains, growth rate unaffected), glycerol consumption, final GABA titer: singles below WT; doubles ΔgabTΔackA 0.46 +/- 0.02, ΔgabTΔmgsA 0.45 +/- 0.01 g/L; ΔmgsAΔackA 0.37 +/- 0.04; CY02_TKO 0.59 +/- 0.04 g/L, productivity 0.13 +/- 0.02 g/L/hr (1.5/1.6-fold vs CY02; 3.9/4.3-fold vs WT).

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Acetate overflow measured in this study (Fig. 4B); knockout phenotypes measured directly (Fig. 6, Table 3).

alternatives.approach: Other (unspecified) knockout targets were considered; ackA/mgsA/gabT chosen for the stated reasons

decision_chain.implementation_detail: Lambda-Red deletion of ackA, mgsA, gabT singly, as three doubles, and as triple (CY02_TKO), in both CY02 and wild-type backgrounds.

result.metric: Growth (lag phase prolonged in ΔackA strains, growth rate unaffected), glycerol consumption, final GABA titer: singles below WT; doubles ΔgabTΔackA 0.46 +/- 0.02, ΔgabTΔmgsA 0.45 +/- 0.01 g/L; ΔmgsAΔackA 0.37 +/- 0.04; CY02_TKO 0.59 +/- 0.04 g/L, productivity 0.13 +/- 0.02 g/L/hr (1.5/1.6-fold vs CY02; 3.9/4.3-fold vs WT).
result.after: Combined triple deletion synergistic in CY02 background only; benefit absent in wild-type background - epistasis with ALE-acquired mutations; gabT deletion most important single contributor.

decision_chain.rule: When a glycerol-adapted E. coli strain with enhanced substrate influx channels excess carbon into acetate overflow during GABA production, delete ackA, mgsA and gabT in combination, because blocking the acetate sink, the methylglyoxal bypass and the GABA shunt redirects carbon toward GABA - validated only in the evolved E. coli W CY02 background; the same deletions did not improve production in the wild-type background, so the rule is background-dependent.

nodes.decision_summary: Switch from M9 + 0.2% glycerol + 50 mg/L yeast extract to amino-acid-rich LB + glycerol; glycerol concentration screen (0-? %; optimum 2% v/v) using growth rate as proxy assuming growth-coupled production; stationary-phase GABA screen of all strains.
nodes.trigger: Final GABA titers in minimal glycerol medium were negligible and identical between WT and CY02 (0.06 g/L), despite improved glycerol uptake.

nodes.decision_summary: Lambda-Red deletion of ackA, mgsA, gabT singly, as three doubles, and as triple (CY02_TKO), in both CY02 and wild-type backgrounds.
nodes.trigger: CY02 exhibited pronounced acetate overflow (EXP8) wiring excess substrate influx to acetate; known risk of methylglyoxal accumulation to cytotoxic levels in FBP-insensitive glpK backgrounds; GABA shunt recycles product into TCA.

nodes.decision_summary: Verify glpK mRNA downregulation across mutants.
nodes.trigger: Transcriptome consistent with cAMP depletion and aerobic acetate overflow phenotype.

edges.evidence: Supports G3P-mediated auto-catabolite repression of the glpFKX operon.

engineering_logic_chain.goal: Construct an Escherichia coli W derivative with improved gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) production from glycerol by combining adaptive laboratory evolution (1300 generations under glycerol limitation) with rational metabolic engineering (deletion of ackA, mgsA, gabT), and decipher the molecular basis of glycerol adaptation (mutation profiling, enzyme kinetics, transcriptomics).
engineering_logic_chain.initial_bottleneck: Glycerol is a non-preferential, low-energy-density carbon source; prior work showed E. coli W among the best GABA producers from glycerol but without optimization (Hou and Kang, 2018).
engineering_logic_chain.hypothesis: Adapt E. coli W to glycerol limitation to improve glycerol utilization and growth as a chassis for growth-coupled GABA production.

rule_provenance.rule: When improving an E. coli host for growth-coupled product formation from the low-energy-density feedstock glycerol, apply serial-batch ALE under glycerol limitation (order of 10^3 generations), because selection enriches substrate-uptake/utilization mutations (e.g., glpK, crp) that raise fitness and feedstock conversion, as validated for E. coli W glycerol utilization and GABA production in this study.

When growth-coupled production of an amino-acid-derived product (GABA) from glycerol stalls in minimal medium, switch to an amino-acid-rich complex medium and re-optimize feedstock concentration using growth rate as proxy, because biosynthetic precursor (L-glutamate) cost and carbon availability, not uptake capacity, limit product formation - demonstrated for E. coli W GABA production.

When a glycerol-adapted E. coli strain with enhanced substrate influx channels excess carbon into acetate overflow during GABA production, delete ackA, mgsA and gabT in combination, because blocking the acetate sink, the methylglyoxal bypass and the GABA shunt redirects carbon toward GABA - validated only in the evolved E. coli W CY02 background; the same deletions did not improve production in the wild-type background, so the rule is background-dependent.
